newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 24.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
- GIVING BIRTH AT 63, THE OLDEST MOTHER IN THE WORLD

The debate over late-life motherhood has been rekindled on the news that a 63 year woman has become the world's oldest mother. The woman was so desperate to have a child she lied about her age at a Los Angeles fertility clinic.
- FUNDS FACE IMRO CALL FOR INSURANCE

In light of the Peter Young affair, city regulators are examining whether new mechanisms are needed to deal with operational risks faced by fund managers. It has been suggested that compulsory insurance is the only means to protect investors against similar occurrences in the future.
- STERLING TAKES FRIGHT IN ELECTION SHADOW

Ahead of the General Election on May 1st investors remain nervous about holding Sterling. Yesterday sterling staged a thin recovery even though dealers said the British currency struggled to attract buyers.
Suggestions that Apple are looking for friendly merger buyers have been denied. Apple's Chairman Gilbert Amelio maintained that the company wishes to remain independent.
- 26M STG FOR MAGNATE AS US FEUD COOLS

The end of a long-running feud is coming to the end in the States as retail magnate Herbert Haft relinquishes control of the multi million dollar retail empire he founded 50 years ago. He will receive 26mn stg in a deal that will bankruptcy of the company.
